title: Quick inference metrics tracker (personal scratchsheet)
content:
Quick personal tracker for small inference experiments — light-weight sheet for comparing latency and cost across quantization and batching strategies. NOT official benchmarking; rough notes for my spike work.

Table: columns = date | model | variant | quant | bs | seq | p50_ms | p95_ms | tokens_per_request | cost_per_1k_tokens_usd | notes

2025-11-04 | redwood-v1-7b | base | fp16 | 1 | 128 | 48 | 95 | 200 | 0.045 | cold-start, single-stream, no KV cache
2025-11-05 | redwood-v1-7b | base | int8 | 1 | 128 | 36 | 72 | 200 | 0.033 | PTQ on A100, minor quality diff on edge-case prompts
2025-11-10 | redwood-v1-7b | opt | int8 | 2 | 128 | 42 | 80 | 400 | 0.027 | batching improved token throughput but p95 rose slightly
2025-11-12 | redwood-v1-7b | opt | int8+kv-cache | 1 | 512 | 28 | 46 | 600 | 0.020 | prefix cache enabled, big win for repeated-history cases
2025-11-15 | redwood-v1-7b | opt | int4 | 1 | 128 | 34 | 68 | 200 | 0.021 | experimental int4 build, watch hallucination on long-context
2025-11-21 | redwood-v1-13b | base | fp16 | 1 | 128 | 72 | 140 | 200 | 0.090 | baseline for 13b model
2025-11-22 | redwood-v1-13b | base | int8 | 1 | 128 | 54 | 110 | 200 | 0.067 | good perf/cost tradeoff for mid-size payloads
2025-11-27 | redwood-v1-13b | opt | int8 | 4 | 128 | 58 | 112 | 800 | 0.034 | batching helps cost per token; tail latency steady
2025-11-30 | redwood-v1-7b | opt | int8 | 8 | 64 | 68 | 170 | 1600 | 0.017 | heavy batching increases throughput but p95 jumps (queueing)
2025-12-01 | redwood-v1-7b | opt | int8 | 1 | 1024 | 24 | 40 | 1400 | 0.018 | long-seq optimized kernels engaged, good p95

Quick observations / heuristics I keep referring to:
- int8 PTQ usually drops p50 by ~20–30% vs fp16 on same hw for batch=1.
- Batching reduces cost_per_1k but risks p95 inflation if queueing not bounded; add max-latency guard.
- KV/prefix caching is the cheapest win for low-latency chat workloads where history repeats.
- int4 is promising for tight cost targets but requires eval on hallucination-sensitive prompts.

Open questions / next mini-runs:
- Repeat the int4 run with a curated eval set (10 prompts) to quantify quality delta (target: <3% regen diff).
- Try sequence-length profiling across real-prod traces to decide default cache TTLs.
- Re-run 13b int8 with per-request dynamic batching (deadline 50ms) to measure p95 tradeoff.

Light checklist (for my spike):
- [x] run int8 baseline on A100 (11/05)
- [x] add KV cache test (11/12)
- [x] test 13b int8 baseline (11/22)
- [ ] int4 quality check (blocked by eval harness)
- [ ] dynamic-batching p95 experiment (to schedule)

Notes-to-self: keep these runs reproducible — commit the small harness script to a personal branch, tag the docker image with run date, and paste the evallog link here when ready. Also ping Priya for the int4 model weight checksum and any known regressions.

Scratch formulas I used here (for my notes):
- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd = (cost_per_infer_usd / tokens_per_request) * 1000  (I approximate cost_per_infer_usd from GCP slot-hour equivalent)
- effective_throughput_tps = tokens_per_request * (1 / p50_seconds)
